key_insight: X^3-OPD teaches large audio-language models to reason better by distilling step-by-step reasoning from a strong text teacher during training, instead of relying on scarce audio reasoning labels. The result is a cross-modal alignment method that directly improves logical reasoning in audio tasks.
problem_solved: Large audio-language models can perceive sounds well, but they still struggle with deep logical reasoning because high-quality audio reasoning data is limited and expensive to collect.
method: Use a powerful text-based teacher model to generate reasoning targets for the audio student.
Train the audio-language student with on-policy alignment, letting it produce its own reasoning trajectories during training.
Distill cross-modal reasoning ability so the student learns to connect audio inputs with structured logical steps rather than only surface-level predictions.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical way to improve reasoning in audio AI without needing massive annotated audio reasoning datasets. Practitioners building speech, sound, and audio-assistant systems can use this framework to make models more capable of multi-step inference and decision-making.
visual_elements: A teacher-student pipeline diagram showing text teacher -> audio student.
A before/after comparison of audio model reasoning quality.
A training loop graphic highlighting on-policy trajectory generation and alignment.
Icons for audio waveforms, text reasoning chains, and distilled knowledge transfer.
paper_title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
paper_authors: Dongjie Fu, Di Cao, Xize Cheng, Zihan Zhang, Wenxu Jia
